For more information see our Privacy StatementNewsHow to Watch the 2025 Masters TournamentBy Nick Pietruszkiewicz| Monday, March 31, 2025It's Tuesday at the Masters, and after a wet day on Monday many players will be stepping onto the course for their first time this Masters week to prepare for the 89th playing of the Tournament. Tonight is the annual Champions Dinner where the menu will be served in 2024 champion Scottie Scheffler's honor. A global audience from more than 200 countries and territories will have the opportunity to watch the Tournament, across multiple platforms, from Augusta National Golf Club. In addition to the thorough coverage available on the Masters App and Masters.com – On The Range, Amen Corner, Featured Groups and more – this year's offerings will include five additional hours of live coverage for the third and final rounds. In addition to Saturday’s CBS broadcast being extended by one hour to match Sunday's final round (2-7 p.m. ET), Paramount+ will debut four live hours from noon-2 p.m. ET on both Saturday and Sunday, which will also stream on Masters.com and the Masters App. First and second round broadcast coverage of the Tournament will be aired by ESPN on Thursday and Friday from 3-7:30 p.m. ET. SiriusXM will handle radio coverage for all four rounds. Spanish-speaking viewers in the United States can follow the action on ESPN Deportes, which will air live coverage of the Tournament. Throughout the Tournament, the Masters will be broadcast live to a global audience from more than 200 countries and territories. The American Forces Network will also broadcast the event to U.S. military installations throughout the world. A full list of networks carrying the 2025 Masters Tournament around the world is available here.New for this year: Mornings at the Masters, hosted by Hally Leadbetter and Roger Steele, will air live from Augusta National on the Masters YouTube channel from Wednesday, April 9th through Sunday, April 13th at 9am ET and focus on lifestyle and cultural elements of the Tournament.Leading into the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday, ESPN will air a one-hour edition of their preview show — Welcome to the Masters. The show will also set up live coverage on Thursday and Friday from 1-3 p.m.Kicking off an extended Masters week on Saturday, April 5 will be the final round of the Augusta National Women’s Amateur on NBC. On Sunday, the Drive, Chip and Putt National Finals will air on Golf Channel.
